title: Queue rules follow user tier
summary:
Queue priority now follows tier and authentication, text caching ignores irrelevant request fields, and GPT Image routing follows user stage.

Nectar requests now skip the queue whether authenticated by token or registered referrer. Other token-authenticated requests enter with a zero interval, while standard queue timing remains for other requests. GPT Image access is checked against authentication status rather than queue bypass.

Text cache keys now ignore authentication and cache-control fields, so otherwise identical requests can use the same cache entry even when those fields differ.

GPT Image requests now route by user stage instead of randomly: Seed uses one endpoint, while Flower and Nectar use another. Failed Turbo and Flux fetches now return an error immediately rather than retrying.
